reason: The cited evidence confirms the as-cast alloy's brittleness under tension (E2) and mentions energy release in related alloys (E1), but provides no support for the key premises that thermomechanical processing can induce a ductile secondary phase, refine grains, or improve ductility in HfZrTiTa0.53, nor that strength and energy release would be preserved.
premises: HfZrTiTa0.53 has limited tensile ductility and uniform elongation in the as-cast state
Cold working plus sub-solvus annealing can refine grains and induce a secondary ductile phase in refractory HEAs
A refined duplex microstructure increases strain-hardening and delays necking, improving uniform elongation
A secondary ductile phase acts as a barrier to crack initiation and propagation
The proposed processing preserves high strength and impact-triggered energy release
